policy.authority: PTO ASL and accepted architecture decisions define numeric semantics; public implementation evidence exposes choices but cannot select them.
policy.profile_boundary: Support restrictions, portable result rules, named target result rules, and bounded implementation-defined behavior must be classified separately.
policy.cpu_role: CPU simulation is an implementation under test and host arithmetic is not a target oracle.
policy.independent_comparison_role: The closed executable-ISA comparison validates identities and bounded structural semantics but does not provide S5-T2 numeric differential results.
policy.no_implicit_choice: A missing profile rule remains open; the generator never chooses the most convenient backend behavior.

decision_questions.title: profile identity and support-versus-semantics boundary
decision_questions.finding: The public contract names CPU, A2A3, and A5 capability profiles and says profiles narrow support, while the numeric contract also exposes target-dependent result variation.
decision_questions.unresolved_rule: Decide whether portable numeric results exist for each domain and which remaining differences are named target-profile rules rather than support restrictions.
acceptance_evidence: accepted profile taxonomy and version identifiers

decision_questions.title: numeric format encodings and target availability
decision_questions.finding: The public type names span IEEE, BF16, FP8, specialized eight-bit, four-bit, and integer carriers, but target availability and conversion paths differ.
decision_questions.unresolved_rule: Freeze every format encoding, supported operation/type pair, widening or reinterpretation rule, and profile rejection before numeric vectors are generated.

decision_questions.title: rounding taxonomy, selection, and tie behavior
decision_questions.finding: The public prose names four directional modes while backend conversion paths expose additional round, odd, part, and saturation combinations.
decision_questions.unresolved_rule: Map every encoded or profile-selected rounding value to an exact result rule, including tie behavior, unsupported combinations, and operation-local overrides.

decision_questions.title: subnormal handling, FTZ, and numeric mode state
decision_questions.finding: The public contract allows default FTZ and names target controls, while implementation evidence includes explicit subnormal handling in selected operations.
decision_questions.unresolved_rule: Define input and result FTZ separately, the architectural visibility and lifetime of numeric mode state, and whether an operation may override default FTZ.

decision_questions.title: NaN, infinity, signed zero, and payload rules
decision_questions.finding: ADR 0050 closes canonical produced NaNs plus comparison and min/max NaN and signed-zero selection for a bounded named-hardware operation set. Published and implementation evidence still distinguish propagation, sentinel, payload, infinity, conversion, reduction, quantization, matrix, and flag/status cases without one complete cross-operation rule.
decision_questions.unresolved_rule: Complete NaN creation beyond comparison and min/max, signaling flag/status behavior, infinity production, and special-value conversion, reduction, quantization, and matrix results.
acceptance_evidence: bit-exact special-value table extending the accepted ADR 0050 checkpoint
binary, unary, conversion, compare, reduction, quantization, and matrix vectors

decision_questions.title: scalar numeric exception flags
decision_questions.finding: The formal scalar surface owns NV, DZ, OF, UF, and NX hooks, but the audited public numeric contract does not define a complete producer, stickiness, or priority rule.
decision_questions.unresolved_rule: Define per-operation flag production, simultaneous flags, stickiness, reset, and trap interaction for every scalar numeric domain.

decision_questions.title: conversion overflow, saturation, wrap, and indefinite results
decision_questions.finding: The public contract records undefined hardware overflow where CPU simulation may saturate, and backend paths also expose non-saturating wrap and target-specific control combinations.
decision_questions.unresolved_rule: Choose a deterministic result or a bounded implementation-defined result set for every source, destination, rounding, saturation, NaN, infinity, and out-of-range combination.
acceptance_evidence: minimum, maximum, one-past, NaN, and infinity vectors

decision_questions.title: elementary-function accuracy and domain behavior
decision_questions.finding: CPU and target implementations use different library, intrinsic, or custom approximation paths, so matching operation names do not establish equal numeric results.
decision_questions.unresolved_rule: Define exact rounding or an explicit accuracy bound, monotonicity requirement, domain errors, and special-value results for division, reciprocal, square root, reciprocal square root, logarithm, exponential, and exponential difference.

decision_questions.title: reduction width, order, ties, and stability
decision_questions.finding: CPU and target reduction trees differ, optimized shapes may change grouping, and selected integer paths widen then narrow with wrap behavior.
decision_questions.unresolved_rule: Freeze accumulation width and order, overflow behavior, NaN and signed-zero selection, arg tie-breaking, partial merge behavior, and stable ordering requirements.
acceptance_evidence: widening, overflow, NaN, zero, and partial-merge vectors

decision_questions.title: quantization and dequantization scale contract
decision_questions.finding: Implementation evidence contains multiple format, shared-exponent, scale, zero-point, clamping, and special-value paths that are not one portable arithmetic rule.
decision_questions.unresolved_rule: Define scale and zero-point encoding, grouping axis and size, exponent selection, rounding, clamping, exceptional sentinels, packing, and inverse dequantization for every accepted format.
acceptance_evidence: NaN, infinity, zero, max, tie, clamp, pack, and round-trip vectors

decision_questions.title: matrix product, accumulation, bias, and MX arithmetic
decision_questions.finding: CPU evidence uses host arithmetic and fused accumulation for selected types, while target paths use matrix hardware and A5 adds MX scale formats.
decision_questions.unresolved_rule: Define product precision, accumulator width, accumulation order, intermediate rounding, saturation, bias order, source accumulator order, MX scale interpretation, and special-value behavior per type tuple.
acceptance_evidence: bias, accumulate, MX scale, overflow, saturation, and exceptional-value vectors

decision_questions.title: bounded implementation-defined numeric behavior
decision_questions.finding: The public contract permits target variation but does not provide a complete allowed-result set or discovery mechanism for each numeric variation point.
decision_questions.unresolved_rule: For every non-portable result, name the selecting profile or visible mode, bound the allowed results, and require generic validation to reject an unknown profile or unconfigured implementation-defined rule.
acceptance_evidence: allowed-result sets for every implementation-defined rule
